s: A media company replicates new objects from an S3 bucket in us-east-1 to a bucket in us-west-2 with S3 Cross-Region Replication. A new contract requires a service-level agreement that most new objects are replicated within 15 minutes. Operations must be alerted about any object that misses that threshold. The bucket already contained 400 million objects before replication was configured, and these objects must also exist in the destination bucket. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)
o: Enable S3 Replication Time Control on the replication rule, and use the replication metrics and the S3 Event Notifications for objects that exceed the 15-minute threshold to alert operations.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source bucket to speed up replication.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point with failover controls across the two buckets.
Run an S3 Batch Replication job to replicate the objects that existed before the replication rule was created.
Schedule an AWS DataSync task every 15 minutes between the buckets to copy any objects that replication missed.

w.y: S3 RTC is the only replication option backed by an SLA (designed for 99.99% within 15 minutes, with a 99.9% SLA). It adds metrics and threshold-missed events for alerting. Live replication never copies objects that existed before the rule, and S3 Batch Replication is the built-in way to backfill them.

o.A: Correct: RTC gives the 15-minute SLA plus metrics and events for objects that miss the threshold.
o.B: Transfer Acceleration speeds up client uploads over the internet. It does nothing for replication and carries no SLA.
o.C: A Multi-Region Access Point routes requests between buckets. It does not replicate data or give a replication SLA.
o.D: Correct: Batch Replication copies the existing objects that live CRR skips.
o.E: DataSync adds a second copy mechanism, has no SLA, and does not satisfy the replication-SLA requirement.
